proposals.title: Where your points go: a per-skill miss ledger that decides the plan
proposals.what:
Server: add `plan.ledger(learner)`. For each of the 19 skills it returns:
- `per_section`: expected questions in a 44-question Math section. This is the domain's published share times the skill's share of its domain. The skill shares go in a new constant `blueprint.SKILL_FREQ`, taken from the College Board question-bank counts in ttp-notes. Examples: Nonlinear functions 258/538 of Advanced Math gives 7.4 a section; Circles 67/348 of Geometry gives 1.3.
- `acc[tier]`: clean first-try accuracy on (template, seed) pairs the student had never seen (R8 clean answers). It is shrunk toward the student's domain accuracy with 4 pseudo-answers.
- `mix`: module 1 at 7/8/7, plus the module-2 mix of the likely route. Use upper (3/8/11) when estimate.mean3 ≥ 580 or target > 580, otherwise lower (11/8/3).
- `misses = Σ per_section·mix·(1−acc)`.
- `worth`: points recovered if acc reached 0.85, using scoring's weights and scoring.fraction_for.
- `data`: the clean answers counted.

Plan tab: a card "Where your points go" at the top of the right column.
- Header: `About 9.4 of 44 questions a section missed`.
- Rows sorted by misses, e.g. `Nonlinear functions · 2.1 of 7.4 missed · worth ~25 pts · 3 sets this week`. Each row has a bar of misses split easy/medium/hard (§2.3 tokens) and a `Low data · 6 answers` tag below 12 clean answers. A row opens /practice/?topics=.

Allocation: topic weight = misses × the focus multiplier (2 / 1 / 0.4), with a floor so every skill appears at least once in 14 days. This replaces `(1.5 − m_d)` and the coach score for plan days, and the SplitBar shows these shares.

Other surfaces:
- Every task's Why gains `Worth about 0.6 questions a section (~9 pts)`.
- The week theme gains `targets 3.1 missed questions`.
- The freeze stores the ledger in plan_days, so Progress can chart `Missed a section 9.4 → 6.8 since Sep 23`, stacked by domain.
- Caption: `Counted from your first answers on questions new to you. Points use this site's scoring, not the College Board's.`
proposals.beats: Their plan claims tasks are 'weighted toward the domains costing the most points'. It shows no number, works at 8 domains, and its weakAreas are fixed at generation. Their accuracy is also polluted by unlimited retries on the same item. Ours puts a checkable number on every one of the 19 skills, measured only on questions the student had never seen, and recomputes it daily. The same number drives the schedule, the Why lines and the Progress chart.
proposals.needs:
- R8 clean-answer flags on attempts (F4).
- blueprint.DOMAIN_SPLIT/TIERS, plus the new SKILL_FREQ constant.
- scoring.fraction_for (already in this spec).
- estimate.mean3 for the route (R16).
- A `ledger` JSON column on plan_days (F4 §2.5).
- plan.py allocation change.

proposals.title: Exam-day forecast from your own learning rate, live in the wizard and on the plan
proposals.what:
Server: add `plan.forecast(cfg, learner)`.
- Per skill, the rate is the gain in clean first-try accuracy per 10 answers: a least-squares slope over the student's last 60 answers in that skill (at least 20 needed).
- The rate is shrunk toward a population prior: the median slope for that skill across all learners' attempts, cached daily in a small `priors` table.
- Returns diminish: acc' = acc + rate·(q/10)·(1−acc)/(1−acc0).
- q is the questions the allocation walk actually plans for that skill up to the exam.
- The projected ledger misses are scored into a section band of ±70.

Wizard GainCard:
- A grey 'Forecast' span on the 200–800 track: `At this plan: 630–690 on Nov 7`.
- Under it, `Reaches 700 with: 70 min × 5 · 45 min × 6 · Dec 5`. Each is a button that applies that change.
- Recomputed by POST /api/plan/preview (≤150 ms).
- PaceTag (the unsourced thresholds in open questions) shows only when there is no data.

Plan view:
- The Score tile adds `Forecast 640–700`, and its chip compares the forecast midpoint with the target: `On track`, `Short by ~20` or `Ahead`.
- The TrajectoryChart draws a grey cone from now to the exam.
- Each BehindBanner option shows its forecast effect.

Below 60 clean answers in total, every place reads `Forecast after 60 answers · 23 so far` instead of numbers. Caption: `A forecast, not a promise: your own rate so far, applied to the questions this plan gives each skill.`
proposals.beats: Their pace line ('about 60 points per week') never says whether that pace is realistic, and nothing in their plan predicts an outcome. Ours answers 'will I make it, and what would it take?' from the student's own measured rate on fresh questions, and turns the answer into one-tap changes. It also resolves our own open question on the PaceTag heuristic.
proposals.needs:
- The ledger (proposal 1).
- A plan.py allocation walk that exposes planned questions per skill.
- The preview endpoint.
- A priors cache (a new small table, F4).
- The band constants from estimate.py (R16).

proposals.title: Trap-proof sets built from your misconception profile
proposals.what:
Server: add `plan.profile(learner)`, which groups the student's misses by trap `norm` (R9) across templates. A family is 'recurring' when it has 2 or more hits.

New counted task kind `trapproof`:
- At most one a day, on practice days while a recurring family is active, 6–10 questions.
- Drill body `{pool:'related', ids:norm, count, task:'D:trapproof'}`. It serves fresh questions from any template whose distractors carry that misconception (the `want` regex walk), including skills where the student has not fallen for it yet.
- Row title: `Trap-proof · “Distributed the minus to the first term only”`.
- Detail: `8 questions across Equivalent expressions, Linear equations, Systems · each hides this wrong answer`.
- Why: `You chose this 4 times in 3 skills; last Sep 21`.

In the session, a right answer on such an item adds the verdict line `Dodged: that mistake was choice C`, using the per-answer `reasons` already returned.

Progress tab card 'Your traps' shows the top 8 families: label, hits, skills and last fallen for. Each has a status:
- `Active`.
- `Quiet 14 d`.
- `Retired`: 3 dodges on fresh items plus check-ins passed.

Each active family also gets a `Trap-proof now · 8` button. A relapse reopens the family.
proposals.beats: Their explanations carry per-question 'Distractor Analysis' prose, but nothing links one mistake across questions, so they cannot find a habit, let alone drill it. Ours hunts the habit across the whole bank with new questions built to tempt exactly that error, and shows when it is gone.
proposals.needs:
- Review's traps `norm` (R9, F4).
- Drill `pool:'related'` and `want` (§2.6, F5).
- A plan.py task kind with Why lines.
- The Review section consumes the same profile for 'same mistake elsewhere'.

proposals.title: Start my day: the whole day's plan as one continuous run
proposals.what:
Today's plan card and the DayPanel get one pill, `Start today · 3 tasks · 45 min`, shown when 2 or more counted tasks are undone.

Server:
- POST /api/plan/{id}/run {day} stores the ordered start bodies of the undone counted tasks as `chain` in the first session's cfg.
- drill_finish on a chained session creates the next session and returns `next_session`.
- Each segment keeps its own `task` tag, so per-task status, Why and Review stay exact.

Runner:
- A day rail above the progress rail with segments `Mistakes 8 · Still fixed? 2 · Focus 18 · Words 6m`. The current segment is orange.
- Between tasks, an in-runner divider card (not a page load): `Mistakes done · 7 of 8 · 2 traps closed`, `Next: Focus set · Circles, Percentages · 18 questions`, then `Continue` (Enter) · `Stop for today`.
- The divider auto-continues after 5 s unless motion is reduced.
- Your own tasks appear in the chain as a check card: `Reading & Writing · 30 min`, with Done / Skip / Later and an optional timer.

Leaving mid-run shows `Resume today · Focus 6 of 18` on Today. The end card shows minutes, questions, right, traps closed and skills graduated, plus `Keep going · 10 more from your biggest leak` (from the ledger).
proposals.beats: On theirs, each task is launched separately from the plan page, and the student returns to the plan to find the next one. Ours does the whole day from one tap, with the plan's structure visible inside the runner.
proposals.needs:
- The S4 runner (day rail, divider card).
- A chained drill_finish (F5/S4).
- Today's plan card (S3).
- Words task launch (S9).
- plan.py run endpoint.

proposals.title: Skills graduate by proof on unseen questions, then come back on a spaced schedule
proposals.what:
Server: a per-skill stage machine in plan.py, stored in a new table plan_skills(plan, topic, stage, since, next_check):
- `Learning`.
- `Proof due`: clean accuracy ≥ 75% over the last 12 answers in that skill and no open trap.
- `Graduated`.
- `Keep-warm`: 4-question mixed-tier checks inside focus sets at +7, +21 and +45 days.
- `Slipped`: under 3 of 4 on a keep-warm check, which returns the skill to Learning.

Proof task:
- Row: `Proof · Circles · 6 questions · medium–hard · timed 9:30`.
- Drill `{topics:[s], tiers:['medium','hard'], count:6, timed:true, minutes:10, task:'D:proof'}`.
- Passing is 5 of 6. The result card reads `Circles graduated` and shows where the freed time went: `+1 set a week to Nonlinear functions`.

Allocation: a graduated skill takes the strong multiplier and keep-warm slots only. The wizard's focus choice is the starting state, and graduation overrides it until the skill slips.

UI:
- A 'Skills ladder' card on the Plan tab (also in step 4's skill rows) shows each skill's stage and dates, e.g. `Circles · Graduated Oct 2 · next check Oct 9`.
- The calendar shows mono `P` / `K` tags on proof and keep-warm days.
- The phase strip shows graduation markers.
proposals.beats: Their weakAreas and strengths are set in the wizard and change only through Rebalance or Rebuild, and nothing is ever finished. Ours makes progress per skill visible, earned and automatic. A proof means something only because every proof question is new to the student, which a finite bank cannot guarantee.
proposals.needs:
- Clean answers (R8).
- Drill tiers/timed/count (§2.6).
- A new plan_skills table (F4).
- The keep_warm pref (§2.7).
- plan.py allocation hook.

proposals.title: Instant plan from your results, tuned on one screen as the real calendar redraws
proposals.what:
Landing, when any data exists: the hero reads `Your plan is ready`. It shows a drafted plan with these defaults:
- The next published SAT at least 21 days out.
- 45 min × Mon–Fri.
- A weekly module on Friday.
- Focus from the ledger.
- mean3 as the current score.
- Target = current + 100.

The hero draws that plan's real first week (a WeekStrip with topics per day) and its forecast band, with `Start this plan` (one tap, POST /api/plan) and `Adjust`.

Adjust, at ≥1080px: one scroll with the four sections as panels (Score · Target & date · Time · Focus), each showing `Suggested` values with a one-line reason. A sticky right column is the actual first two weeks (two WeekStrips with topics), plus totals and the forecast. It redraws from POST /api/plan/preview within 250 ms of each change, and changed days flash an ink outline. `Create` is enabled from the start. Below 1080px the four-step stepper stays.

Preview returns `weeks[0..1]` with tasks.
proposals.beats: Theirs takes 4 steps, then a fake 'about a minute' build screen that failed 3 times out of 3, with one plan per billing cycle. Ours gives a working plan in one tap, and every setting shows its effect on the actual days before the student commits.
proposals.needs:
- Preview extended with week tasks (plan.py).
- Ledger and forecast (proposals 1 and 2).
- UI.calendar/WeekStrip components (F1).
- Landing and wizard (S7).

proposals.title: Checkpoints: the same test with new numbers, so progress is measured
proposals.what:
The plan's test task becomes a checkpoint at each phase boundary (end of Build, end of Sharpen), and on every third test day otherwise.
- Title: `Checkpoint · twin of your Sep 25 module`.
- Start: POST /api/mock/new {like:<first plan test sid>, task}. Same template, tier and position in every slot, on new seeds (Tests' twin, §3.4).

Result, on the report and in the DayPanel: `Checkpoint 2 · 13 → 18 of 22 on the same question types`. A slot-by-slot strip counts `right now, wrong then 6 · wrong now, right then 1 · both wrong 3` and lists the misconceptions still hit.

Other surfaces:
- The TrajectoryChart draws checkpoint pairs as linked marks, distinct from ordinary tests.
- The Score status chip and drift prefer checkpoints when present.
- A Progress row reads `Checkpoints: 13 → 16 → 18`.
proposals.beats: Their retakes re-serve the same paper, whose answers the student remembers, and they spend a paid retake quota. Scores on different papers are not comparable either. A twin is an equal form built on demand, so the gain is real.
proposals.needs:
- Tests' twin (`like`, §3.4).
- A test-task option `twin_of` in plan.py.
- The report's twins comparison (S6).
- UI.bandChart (F1).

proposals.title: Route-up guard: for targets above 580, train and track the module-1 route
proposals.what:
When the target is above LOWER_ROUTE_CEILING (580), plan.py tracks routing.
- It records how many of the student's recent module-1s routed up (≥ ROUTE_UP_AT, 14 of 22).
- It computes module-1 readiness: expected right answers on a 7/8/7 module 1, from the ledger.
- The Score tile shows `Routes up 2 of last 3 · needs 14 of 22`.

When readiness is under 14.5, Sharpen adds a weekly task:
- `Module 1 drill · 22 questions · 7 easy / 8 medium / 7 hard · 35 min`.
- Drill `{mix:'blueprint', count:22, timed:true, minutes:35, task}`.
- Why: `Your last module 1 had 12 right. 14 routes you up, and 700 needs the upper module.`

The test DayPanel result adds `Would have routed up with 2 of your easy misses` (from the report's what-if).
proposals.beats: Their plan never mentions routing, although for any target above about 580 it is the biggest structural fact: the lower second module caps Math at 580 (the College Board's own figure). Ours names the threshold, tracks it and trains it.
proposals.needs:
- scoring.ROUTE_UP_AT and LOWER_ROUTE_CEILING.
- blueprint.TIERS.
- The route stored on test results.
- Drill `mix:'blueprint'` (§2.6).
- The report's what-if (S6).

proposals.title: Print the week with its real questions, then bubble the answers in
proposals.what:
PlanMenu `Print…` opens a dialog:
- Range: `Today` · `Next 3 days` · `This week`.
- `Include answer key and explanations` (on by default).
- `Include mistakes and rechecks`.

On print, the server fixes those future days' items: each day's fix, recheck and focus tasks get exact (template, seed) lists in a new plan_days.items column. The online task then serves the same items (`pool:'items', exact:true`), so paper and screen agree.

Each printed day has:
- A header, e.g. `Thu Oct 1 · Focus · Circles, Percentages · 45 min`.
- Numbered questions with figures and space to work.
- A bubble grid (A–D, grid-in boxes).
- A short code with a QR, `/p/7KQ2M`.

The last pages hold the key: each answer, each wrong option's misconception and a one-line rationale.

/p/<code> opens a fast answer grid (tap A–D per number, type grid-ins). `File answers` grades them, opens and closes traps, marks the day's tasks done (source 'worksheet') and offers repairs online for the misses.
proposals.beats: They have no print, and their export button is dead. Our spec's Print is only a topic list. A finite bank can print its questions once; ours prints fresh ones every time and still files every answer into the plan.
proposals.needs:
- The Review/Practice worksheet endpoint and print CSS (§3.3, §3.9).
- deps.access (R19).
- A plan_days.items column (F4).
- A short code from R18 sets kind 'items'.
- A small answer-grid page.

proposals.title: Bluebook bridge: log an official practice test and get look-alikes for every miss
proposals.what:
The quick-add chip `+ Official Bluebook practice test` creates an own task of kind `outside_test`. Marking it Done opens a sheet:
- Math score (200–800) and, optionally, R&W.
- `Which Math questions did you miss?`: a 1–44 number grid.
- For each picked number: skill chips (19, grouped by domain), then an optional `What went wrong?` list with that skill's named misconceptions (the Log-a-mistake step 3), or `Not sure`.

Save:
- Posts each miss to POST /api/mistakes/log (source 'outside', origin `Bluebook Test 4 · Q12`).
- Sends the score to estimate.py as an `outside` sitting, drawn on the trajectory as a diamond.

The next practice day gets a fix task `From Bluebook Test 4 · 6 misses · 12 look-alikes`, with 2 fresh items per logged type. Drift and the forecast consider the official score, and Progress shows `Official tests 2 · last 640`.
proposals.beats: Their plan can schedule only their own papers, so an official test is invisible to it. No finite bank can produce look-alikes of an official question. We can, by skill and named misconception, with new numbers.
proposals.needs:
- The Shell quick sheet's Log a mistake and POST /api/mistakes/log (§2.7).
- estimate.py accepting outside sittings (R16).
- A custom-task kind in plan.py.

proposals.title: Weekly check-in: last week's result and next week's plan on one sheet
proposals.what:
The sheet opens on the first visit in a new plan week, or from `Review week` on the WeekStrip.

Left, `Week 3`:
- Days done 4/5.
- 3h 10m of 3h 45m.
- 212 questions · 74%.
- Missed a section 8.1 → 7.2.
- Graduated `Circles`.
- 1 trap retired.
- Checkpoint 13 → 18.

Right, `Week 4`: seven columns editable in place.
- A minutes select per day.
- Tap a day to make it rest or off.
- Drag the test to another day.
- Per-day topics with `Swap`.
- `Forecast 640–700 → 650–705` updates live.

`Keep week 4` takes one tap. `Apply` sends all edits as day overrides in one batch (PUT /api/plan/{id}/days [..]), with a toast that has Undo. `week_seen` is stored per plan, so the sheet shows once.
proposals.beats: Their week is a theme sentence plus a move to a later day in the same week, and anything bigger means Rebalance or Rebuild. Ours reviews the week and fixes the next one in under a minute, with the outcome shown.
proposals.needs:
- Week stats in plan.py.
- A batch day-override endpoint.
- The preview forecast (proposal 2).

proposals.title: Your day in your inbox: today's tasks and the first question, answerable from the email
proposals.what:
Settings (§4.3) and wizard step 3 get two switches, off by default:
- `Email me today's plan at 07:00`, for a verified email only.
- `Weekly summary to`, with a parent or tutor address. It sends week stats and the progress link (R18).

The daily email contains:
- `Thu Oct 1 · 45 min · Mistakes 8 · Focus: Circles, Percentages`, and the streak at stake.
- Question 1 of today's focus set, rendered as HTML with its figure as an image. The focus session is pre-created at send time, and the first MC item is used if item 1 is a grid-in.
- Four option buttons. Each is a signed single-use link /a/<token>?o=B (the token maps to session and qid and expires in 24 h). It opens the session with that answer filed and its verdict and named mistake shown.
- `Open today's plan`.

Every email has an unsubscribe link.
proposals.beats: They collect 'Preferred time: Evening' and use it for nothing. They send no reminders and give parents no digest. Ours starts the day's work from the inbox in one tap. The answer is filed because the question is generated for that student that morning.

- `Compare` puts two plans side by side, with a settings diff and outcomes.
- `Save as scenario` stores an unactivated plan with its forecast, so a student can weigh Oct 3 against Nov 7 before switching.

parity_gaps.spec_says: `Today's plan · 2 of 4 done · 33 min left`, a main row with its pill, compact rows, checkboxes for own tasks, Full plan, and Day done with Keep going.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It matches their dashboard card: counts, minutes left, All done, Full Plan and checkboxes.
parity_gaps.upgrade:
- `Start my day` runs the whole day in one continuous run (proposal).
- Minute chips `10m · 20m · as planned · +30m` re-deal today by ledger worth and queue what they displace, using the Day override already specified. This surfaces the buried `Change today's time…` control.

parity_gaps.spec_says: A fresh adaptive module or section on test days, `Make it a section` on long days, and a report on done.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: Their plan also has 'Practice test · Start test'. Freshness beats their finite shelf, but the task ends at the score.
parity_gaps.upgrade:
- Checkpoints as twin tests (proposal).
- An automatic `Debrief` task on the next study day: the test's misses with the misconception behind each chosen option and 2 twins each, counted, and linked to the report.
- In Final, schedule Compete's Season Final (a timed full section one week before the SAT, against everyone) as the plan's dress rehearsal.

parity_gaps.spec_says: A fixed table of phase × target band giving tier lists (Build / Sharpen / Final).
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: A rule by target band is the same kind of setting as their 'Difficulty Level: Adaptive / Fixed'. It ignores the student's measured level on each question type.
parity_gaps.upgrade:
- Per template, serve the edge tier: the lowest tier where the student's clean first-try accuracy over its last 6 is under 80%. Floors come from the phase (Final ≥ medium). Add adaptive:true inside sets (R33).
- When the target is above 580, Sharpen uses the upper module-2 mix (3/8/11).

parity_gaps.spec_says: Toasts with a 5 s Undo for skip, move, mark, remove, day off and archive.
parity_gaps.why_only_parity: It is their toast list with an Undo added. After 5 s, edits made over weeks cannot be seen or reverted.
parity_gaps.upgrade:
A `Changes` log in the PlanMenu:
- Every edit (move, skip, day off, minutes, focus, fit-to-minutes, drift accepted), with its date.
- Revert on each row, applied as an override removal.
